target_customer: College students and groups of six or more, plus corporate clients, who need on demand group rides
problem: Groups must book a charter days ahead with a 5 hour minimum or split across rideshare cars.
business_model: Per rider fare on 15 passenger vans booked through an app, with QR code check in and group payment

founders.name: Matthew Iommi
education: Economics and Business, Texas A&M University
previous_startups: Bought and ran a shuttle service formerly known as Rockin J's while a student (per Dallas Innovates style coverage in search results)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch in February 2025 gives his age as 28; birth year not stated.

founders.name: Justin Rath
founders.background_notes: Described as childhood best friend of Iommi; education not found.

competitors.name: Uber Charter
competitors.what: Party bus and van booking via Uber with US Coachways
competitors.traction_then: Reported by TechCrunch as quietly failing

competitors.name: Uber and Lyft
competitors.what: Ride hail apps requiring splitting groups across cars

technical_complexity.rationale: A dispatch and booking app with QR check in is standard engineering; the hard part is vehicle operations and driver supply.

defensibility.rationale: College campus familiarity and ridership data help, but vans can be rented and Uber could add large vehicles.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Uber Charter launched in 2022 and failed per TechCrunch; Fetii grew to 68 cities in six states by February 2025.

market_need_then: The YC launch post claims over $1M gross revenue in 2021, a $5M+ run rate, 510k passengers and profitability, with three Texas cities. Fares average about $5 per person.

branding.name_origin: Described by TechCrunch (2025) as a French Oceanic term meaning an extension of one's family; other outlets call it a Pacific islands word for extended family.

identity.visual_style: Branded vans recognizable on campus (Arizona State report)

branding.brand_signature: Branded 15 passenger vans recognizable on college campuses
branding.community_and_virality: Student press coverage at Texas A&M, UT Austin and ASU; usage driven by college word of mouth.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong campus presence and student press, but no evidence of iconic status; the family meaning fits the group positioning.

outcome_analysis: Fetii grew from a bootstrapped campus van service into a group rideshare platform claiming profitability at the batch and 200,000 passengers a month across 68 cities by 2025. It raised a $7.35M seed led by Mark Cuban only in 2025, so growth was largely self funded. Uber's group charter attempt failed, which left the niche open.
notes: CB Insights labels the February 2025 round Series A; TechCrunch, the company and other trackers say seed. Total raised estimates vary ($5M to $14.3M) and are unverified. Founding year given as 2019, 2020 and 2022 across sources; YC says 2020. Fetii homepage fetch returned only a title. Competitor sources are from 2025 articles describing 2022 events. Iommi's prior shuttle purchase comes from search result snippets, not an opened page.
